Name: Audit Logging
Engineering Requirement: Recommended engineering practice: select security-relevant events and capture actor/action/time/resource/outcome; protect logs against unauthorized modification and review them under documented policy
Verification Method: Test event coverage and log access restrictions; inspect alert handling and evidence retention against the scoped control design
Gotcha: Write-once storage and a separate store are implementation options not established universal SOC2 mandates; detailed criteria mapping remains unverified
Penalty: SOC2 is an assurance report rather than certification; deficiencies may affect the report or contracts rather than incur an automatic regulatory fine

Name: Encryption at Rest
Engineering Requirement: For HIPAA regulated entities evaluate ePHI encryption through risk analysis; implement when reasonable and appropriate or document the permitted alternative/rationale; select other encryption and key-management controls for applicable scope
Verification Method: Inspect encryption coverage and key access; review HIPAA addressable-specification decisions; verify applicable PCI requirements and SOC2 control commitments separately
Gotcha: HIPAA addressable does not mean optional; universal AES-256 and 90-day rotation and field-level encryption mandates were not established; detailed PCI and SOC2 mapping remains unverified
Penalty: HIPAA enforcement is circumstance-dependent; SOC2 reporting and PCI contractual consequences are separate

Name: Encryption in Transit
Engineering Requirement: For applicable PCI DSS cryptographic protections use strong cryptography with secure TLS configuration; monitor evolving threats and update implementations; map SOC2 controls to engagement scope separately
Verification Method: Scan enabled protocols and cipher suites; test certificate validation and renewal; inspect negotiated configurations rather than version labels alone
Gotcha: PCI SSC does not prescribe a TLS version list; SSL and vulnerable early TLS including 1.0/1.1 are not strong cryptography; mTLS is a design choice rather than a universal mandate
Penalty: A TLS configuration alone does not establish PCI compliance or a SOC2 assurance conclusion

Name: Access Control (RBAC/ABAC)
Engineering Requirement: HIPAA regulated entities authorize access to ePHI for appropriate users and roles; RBAC or ABAC and least privilege are implementation approaches; align SOC2 controls to scoped objectives
Verification Method: Test authorization and termination; review human and service-account permissions at a documented risk-based cadence; inspect access records
Gotcha: Quarterly reviews and a particular access-control model are not established universal mandates; detailed SOC2 criteria mapping remains unverified
Penalty: HIPAA violations may trigger enforcement; SOC2 deficiencies may affect the assurance report or contracts

Name: Data Retention and Deletion
Engineering Requirement: For applicable processing define purpose-based retention and erasure workflows; GDPR controllers respond without undue delay within one month; covered CCPA businesses act on verifiable deletion requests within 45 days
Verification Method: Test request routing and deletion propagation; record lawful retention exceptions; track deadline and extension notices
Gotcha: GDPR permits two further months where justified; CCPA permits one further 45-day extension when reasonably necessary; notify within the initial period; assess backups and legal holds rather than promise immediate universal purge
Penalty: Applicable privacy-law enforcement is case-specific; erasure is not absolute

Name: Consent Management
Engineering Requirement: Identify the applicable GDPR lawful basis per purpose; when relying on consent record freely given specific informed unambiguous agreement and enable easy withdrawal; covered CCPA businesses support sale/sharing opt-out including GPC
Verification Method: Test purpose-specific consent records and withdrawal propagation; test GPC and sale/sharing suppression where applicable
Gotcha: Consent is not required for every GDPR processing operation; explicit consent is required only in specified cases; CCPA is not a blanket opt-in regime; special-category and children's data need separate assessment
Penalty: Applicable privacy-law enforcement depends on scope and infringement

Name: Data Breach Notification
Engineering Requirement: GDPR controllers notify the authority without undue delay and where feasible within 72 hours of awareness unless risk is unlikely; notify individuals without undue delay for likely high risk subject to exceptions; HIPAA covered entities notify individuals of unsecured PHI breaches without unreasonable delay and within 60 days of discovery
Verification Method: Exercise jurisdiction-specific runbooks; record awareness/discovery and risk assessment; retain notification or non-notification evidence
Gotcha: GDPR processors notify controllers without undue delay; HIPAA business associates notify covered entities without unreasonable delay within 60 days; HHS and media thresholds have distinct rules; do not treat maximum periods as waiting periods
Penalty: Notification failures may trigger applicable regulatory enforcement; no universal per-incident fine

Name: PCI DSS Network Segmentation
Engineering Requirement: Recommended scope-management practice: map the cardholder data environment and connected or security-impacting systems; where segmentation is used validate claimed isolation against applicable PCI DSS requirements
Verification Method: Review data flows and network rules; test reachability and segmentation effectiveness; confirm assessment-specific testing obligations with the assessor
Gotcha: Do not infer compliance or failure from flat-network topology alone; segmentation necessity and exact testing cadence were not verified from the accessible standard text
Penalty: Consequences depend on payment-program and contractual arrangements; no universal per-incident fine established

Name: PHI Access Controls
Engineering Requirement: For covered entities and business associates implement authorized access and authentication for ePHI systems; record and examine system activity; apply minimum necessary where applicable
Verification Method: Review access authorizations and audit records; test access termination and authentication; verify required business associate agreements
Gotcha: Security Rule covers ePHI rather than all health data; minimum necessary has Privacy Rule exceptions; a BAA does not replace safeguards
Penalty: HIPAA enforcement depends on the violation and circumstances; no fixed per-control penalty

Name: Vulnerability Management
Engineering Requirement: Recommended practice: inventory software and identify vulnerabilities; prioritize remediation by risk and track closure; separately apply verified PCI DSS patching and scanning requirements and scoped SOC2 commitments
Verification Method: Inspect scan coverage and remediation evidence; track deadlines by their actual contractual or standard basis; retest fixes
Gotcha: A universal 30-day CVE deadline and mandatory SBOM were not established; detailed PCI patch deadlines and ASV scope/cadence remain unverified rather than optional
Penalty: Unresolved vulnerabilities create exposure; assessment and contractual consequences depend on applicable requirements

Name: Change Management
Engineering Requirement: Recommended practice: document and authorize production changes with risk-appropriate testing and deployment evidence; maintain a controlled emergency-change path
Verification Method: Sample approvals and test evidence; trace deployments to authorized changes; review emergency exceptions and privileged actions
Gotcha: A change advisory board and a 24-hour retrospective deadline are not established universal SOC2 mandates; detailed criteria mapping remains unverified
Penalty: Control deficiencies may affect the SOC2 assurance report or contracts; no automatic per-change fine

Name: Data Residency
Engineering Requirement: Map applicable localization obligations separately from GDPR transfers; for Chapter V transfers use applicable adequacy or appropriate safeguards such as SCCs with transfer assessment and supplementary measures where needed; derogations are exceptional
Verification Method: Review recipient and subprocessor locations including remote access; verify transfer mechanism scope and continuing validity; inspect data flows and transfer assessments
Gotcha: GDPR does not impose blanket EEA-only storage; regional hosting alone does not resolve transfers; adequacy is not the only route and SCC signature alone is insufficient
Penalty: Unlawful transfers may trigger corrective measures and penalties under applicable law

Name: Secure Software Development
Engineering Requirement: Use NIST SSDF as recommended secure-development guidance; select design review and code review and security testing practices for the software risk; separately map applicable PCI obligations and scoped SOC2 controls
Verification Method: Review secure-development evidence and remediation tracking; test selected pipeline gates and exception handling
Gotcha: Every-PR scanning and annual training are not established universal cross-framework mandates; NIST recommendations alone do not prove SOC2 or PCI compliance; detailed mappings remain unverified
Penalty: Software weaknesses create exposure; assessment and contractual consequences depend on applicable requirements

Name: Business Continuity / DR
Engineering Requirement: Recommended practice: define recovery objectives from business needs and scoped availability commitments; maintain recovery procedures and exercise restoration at a justified cadence
Verification Method: Measure restoration against documented RPO/RTO; record exercise results and corrective actions; check dependencies and backup recovery
Gotcha: An annual drill is not established here as a universal SOC2 mandate; availability scope and detailed criteria mapping require confirmation
Penalty: Recovery failures create business risk; control deficiencies may affect the scoped SOC2 report or contracts

Name: Third-Party Risk Management
Engineering Requirement: Recommended practice: inventory relevant service providers and assess risks and contractual responsibilities; review assurance evidence within its actual scope; separately implement applicable GDPR processor-contract obligations
Verification Method: Review vendor dependencies and report scope/period/exceptions; verify contractual safeguards and documented reassessment triggers
Gotcha: A vendor SOC2 report does not certify your compliance; blanket annual review and automatic shared liability are unsupported; GDPR subprocessor authorization/contracts are separate legal duties; SOC2 mapping remains unverified
Penalty: Consequences depend on scoped controls and contracts and applicable law; vendor incidents do not imply automatic shared liability

Name: Privacy by Design and Default
Engineering Requirement: GDPR controllers implement appropriate safeguards at design time and during processing; by default process only personal data necessary for each purpose including amount and accessibility and storage duration
Verification Method: Review collection schemas and default permissions; test optional fields and retention settings; retain design assessments
Gotcha: Minimization is not merely encryption or pseudonymization; technical controls support accountability but do not automatically certify compliance
Penalty: Failure may trigger GDPR corrective measures or penalties depending on circumstances

Name: Data Protection Impact Assessment
Engineering Requirement: GDPR controllers assess planned processing before it begins and perform a DPIA where likely high risk to rights and freedoms; document necessity and proportionality and mitigations; consult the authority before processing if residual risk remains high
Verification Method: Record DPIA screening decisions; check competent authority lists; review mitigations and reassess when processing risks change
Gotcha: A security threat model alone is not a DPIA; not every project needs a DPIA and not every DPIA needs prior consultation
Penalty: Failure may trigger GDPR corrective measures or penalties depending on circumstances

Name: Data Subject Access and Portability
Engineering Requirement: GDPR controllers facilitate access requests and provide applicable information and a copy of personal data; portability applies to automated processing based on consent or contract for data provided by the individual; support machine-readable export
Verification Method: Test identity checks and secure export delivery; inspect export completeness and third-party redaction; track the one-month response period and justified extension notices
Gotcha: Access and portability differ; portability includes observed data but not inferred data; protect others' rights and directly transfer only where technically feasible
Penalty: Failure may trigger GDPR corrective measures or penalties depending on circumstances
